chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal and Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Ibrahim ibn al-Sindi, from Yunus ibn Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The loan of the believer is a booty, and it hastens the recompense. If he is affluent, he will pay you back, and if he dies before that, you will count it as Zakat for yourself.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and economic significance of lending money to a believer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the act of lending to a believer from a mere financial transaction to a spiritual investment, describing it as 'booty' (ghanimah) due to its guaranteed reward. The narration provides a unique jurisprudential insight: if the borrower dies insolvent, the outstanding debt is not lost but is counted by God as Zakat for the lender, thereby transforming a potential loss into an act of charity. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the social solidarity of the community, where financial support for believers is viewed as a means of purifying wealth and securing divine favor.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal and Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Ibrahim Bin Al Sindy, from Yunus Bin Ammar who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘A loan of the Believer is a booty, and it hastens the Recompense. If he (borrower) is affluent, he would fulfil it, and if he were to die before that, it would be Reckoned with him (the lender) as being from the Zakāt’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal and al-Hajjal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from Ibrahim al-Sindiy from Yunus ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once heard abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say,
’Lending a loan to a believer is a great gain which hastens reward. If he earns, he pays you back; but if he dies before paying, you can count it as payment of Zakat.’”
